title: Why the angel first said “Hail, full of grace”

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 12, cols. A-B (PDF p. 36)

source_text: Convenienter igitur Angelus sanctae Mariae virgini, primo omnium, illud, Ave gratia plena, Dominus tecum, praesignificavit: quoniam cum ipsa totus gratiae thesaurus reconditus erat. Ex omnibus enim generationibus, haec sola virgo, sancta corpore et spiritu extitit; solaque fert eum, qui verbo omnia portat. Et non solum admirationem nobis parit, sanctissimae illius in corpore pulchritudo; sed et virtutes animae eius.
pass_a_gloss: Fittingly (convenienter) therefore the Angel to holy Mary the virgin, first of all (primo omnium), that (word), Hail full of grace (ave gratia plena), the Lord with you, foretold/announced beforehand (praesignificavit): since with her the whole treasure of grace (totus gratiae thesaurus) was stored away (reconditus erat). For from all generations this virgin alone stood out (extitit) holy in body and spirit (sancta corpore et spiritu); and she alone bears (fert) Him, who by the word (verbo) carries (portat) all things. And not only does it bring forth (parit) admiration (admiratio) for us, the beauty (pulchritudo) of that most holy one in body; but also the virtues (virtutes) of her soul (anima).

choices.choice: 'sancta corpore et spiritu' matches the Vulgate of 1 Corinthians 7:34, said of the unmarried virgin; cited.
'qui verbo omnia portat' matches Hebrews 1:3 ('portansque omnia verbo virtutis suae'); cited.
'praesignificavit' with 'primo omnium' rendered 'announced first of all'.

pass_b_english: Fittingly, then, the Angel announced first of all to the holy Virgin Mary that word: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you (Luke 1:28), since the whole treasure of grace was stored up with her. For of all the generations this Virgin alone was holy in body and in spirit (1 Corinthians 7:34), and she alone carries Him who carries all things by His word (Hebrews 1:3). And it is not only the beauty of that most holy one in body that fills us with wonder, but also the virtues of her soul.
